title: Register your employment related securities scheme
text:
Important deadlines

 If you do not notify HMRC of your employment related securities ( ERS ) scheme by the following deadlines, you risk losing any tax benefits for you and your employees. 

 Tax-advantaged schemes

 You should register new tax-advantaged schemes by 6 July following the tax year they were set up.

 If you miss this deadline, you’ll need to follow the late registration process . 

 Find out how employment related securities work if you’re an employer , including how tax-advantaged share schemes work.

 For Enterprise Management Incentives (EMI)

 For Enterprise Management Incentives (EMI) options granted before 6 April 2024 you must tell us within 92 days of the date of grant.

 If the options are granted after 6 April 2024, you must tell us by 6 July following the end of the tax year in which the grant is made. For example, you should have told us by 6 July 2026 for an option that was granted between 6 April 2025 and 5 April 2026.

 Non-tax-advantaged schemes

 You should register your non-tax-advantaged scheme by 6 July following the tax year when the first reportable event happened (such as acquiring or disposing of securities, or assigning or releasing securities options).

 For example, you should have registered by 6 July 2026 if the first reportable event happened between 6 April 2025 and 5 April 2026.

 You do not need to submit an ERS end of year return for a reportable event if all the following apply to the non-tax-advantaged scheme:

 • the company — or any other company in the same group or under the same ownership — is not registered for PAYE

 • the company does not need to operate PAYE for the reportable event or for anything else it does

 When an employee is employed by an Employer of Record ( EoR ), the EoR remains responsible for submitting the required returns.

 Find out how employment related securities work if you’re an employer , including how non-tax-advantaged share schemes work.

 Before you register 

 Before you can register your ERS scheme, you must first register as an employer .

 If you need to register as an employer, it can take up to 30 working days to get your PAYE reference number.

 Once you have an employer PAYE reference number, you must enrol for and activate the PAYE online service for employers .

 Add the PAYE service to HMRC Online Services 

 You’ll need your PAYE reference and Accounts Office reference. These are included in the letter from HMRC confirming your registration.

 • 
 Sign in to HMRC Online Services for employers or create an account.

 • 
 Select ‘Add a tax, duty or scheme now’. 

 • 
 Select ‘Employers or intermediaries, for example PAYE for employers or CIS’. 

 • 
 Select ‘PAYE for employers’. 

 • 
 Complete the information required on screen.

 Once you’ve enrolled, we’ll send you an activation code in the post. You must use this to activate your account within 28 days of enrolling.

 Register your ERS scheme

 Once you’ve added the PAYE online service, you can register your ERS scheme with us.

 • 
 Sign in to HMRC Online Services for employers . 

 • 
 Go to the section ‘Employment related securities ( ERS )’.

 • 
 Select ‘Register or view your schemes and arrangements’.

 • 
 Select the ERS scheme type you want to register and select ‘Next’. 

 • 
 Fill in the self-certification declaration. 

 • 
 Sign in again to complete your registration.

 HMRC will issue an ERS Scheme reference number online within 7 days of registering your ERS scheme. You will be able to find this on your HMRC Online Services by viewing the ‘Employment related securities ( ERS )’ section and selecting ‘View schemes and arrangements’.

 After you’ve registered 

 You must either:

 • submit your ERS  return

 • submit a nil return — if you have nothing to report

 You must submit a return or nil return by 6 July following the end of the tax year or you may have to pay a penalty.

 How to get an agent authorised to submit ERS  returns

 If you ask an agent to manage your ERS returns, they must complete the Online Agent Authorisation process. Find out how to use the Online Agent Authorisation to get authorised as a tax agent .

 Agents will only be able to view and file returns on employment related securities schemes that are already registered. They will not be able to register or end a scheme.
changeNote: The ‘Non-tax-advantaged schemes’ section has been updated with information about when you do not need to submit an employment related securities return.
